start.confirmDescription: This page starts from the {name} preset, which replaces your current setup in this browser. Share or download your own config first if you want to keep it.

addPlugin.title: Add a plugin
addPlugin.description: Plugins add rules for a language, framework or tool. Add as many as you need; each one is installed as its own package.

welcome.title: Build an ESLint config in a minute
welcome.body: This tool writes a ready-to-use eslint.config.mjs for you. Everything happens in your browser and is saved there, so you can come back to it. Here is a quick look at the four parts.

setup.title: 1. Start from your stack
setup.body: Choose your ESLint version, then pick a preset that matches your project. A preset fills in the plugins and sensible defaults. You can also set global variables and ignored paths here, or start over from a blank config.

plugins.title: 2. Choose your plugins
plugins.body: These are the plugins in your config. Select one to edit it, remove it with the cross, or use Add plugin to browse everything available with a description of what each one checks.

rules.title: 3. Tune the rules
rules.body: Tick a plugin's shared configs to turn on its recommended rules. Then set any individual rule to Off, Warn or Error, and open Options where a rule has them. Use the Changed filter to see only what you altered.

output.title: 4. Take your config
output.body: Your config updates as you go. Copy, download or share a link to it from the Config file view, and switch to Install for the command that adds the packages it needs.

share.invalidTitle: This link could not be opened
share.invalidDescription: The shared config is incomplete or from an incompatible version. Your own setup is unchanged.
share.confirmDescription: It replaces your current setup in this browser. Share or download your own config first if you want to keep it.

stack.title: Pick your stack
stack.body: Start from a preset for JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Next.js with Tailwind CSS, Express or NestJS, and choose ESLint 9 or ESLint 10.

tune.title: Add plugins and tune the rules
tune.body: Add plugins from the catalog and switch their shared configs on or off. Set any rule to off, warn or error and edit its options; each rule shows what your configs already set.

ship.title: Copy, install and lint
ship.body: Copy or download eslint.config.mjs, run the install command for npm, pnpm, yarn or bun, then run npx eslint . in your project.

about.pluginsDescription: Each plugin's rule list is read from its published package, so rule names, recommended settings and deprecations match the version you install.

flatConfig.question: What is an ESLint flat config?
flatConfig.answer: It is the configuration format ESLint uses from version 9: one eslint.config.js (or .mjs, .ts) file that exports an array of config objects. It replaces .eslintrc files, and plugins are imported as ordinary JavaScript modules instead of being resolved by name.

migrate.question: How do I migrate from .eslintrc to a flat config?
migrate.answer: Paste your .eslintrc.json into Import .eslintrc above the editor: it maps extends, plugins, environments and rules onto the generator and lists anything it could not carry over. ESLint's own npx @eslint/migrate-config .eslintrc.json is the alternative for a mechanical conversion.

version.question: Should I use ESLint 9 or ESLint 10?
version.answer: Both use flat config. ESLint 10 removes the old eslintrc format entirely, and some plugins have not declared support for it yet. The generator checks which ESLint versions each plugin supports and warns you before you install one that does not.

typescript.question: Does it support TypeScript and type-aware rules?
typescript.answer: Yes. When you enable a typescript-eslint config that needs type information, the output adds the projectService parser setup and turns type-aware rules off for plain JavaScript files.

next.question: Can I use it for Next.js and Tailwind CSS?
next.answer: Yes. The Next.js + Tailwind preset combines the Next.js, React, React Hooks, jsx-a11y and Tailwind CSS plugins with typescript-eslint, import sorting, Vitest and Stylistic. Remove any of them or add more from the catalog.

privacy.question: Is my configuration stored anywhere?
privacy.answer: Only in your own browser's local storage. There is no account, server or database. A share link carries the config after the # in the URL, a part browsers never send to a server.

free.question: Is it free?
free.answer: Yes. It is free to use, and the source code is on <link>GitHub</link> under the MIT license.

about.faqDescription: Short answers about flat config, migrating and how the generator works. Something missing? <link>Open an issue on GitHub</link>.

import.replaceNote: Importing replaces your current setup in this browser. JavaScript and YAML configs are not supported: convert them to JSON first.
